relations.myth: Creation and ordering of the Moon
relations.note: Ahura Mazdā creates the Moon and establishes its waxing and waning.
They hold Māh’s glory and distribute it over Mazda-created earth.

relations.myth: Invocation of Moon and primordial Bull
relations.note: Māh and the uniquely created Bull are jointly invoked in the Avestan hymn.

relations.myth: Moon preserves the primordial Bull’s seed
relations.note: Māh houses and purifies the dead primordial bovine’s generative seed.

relations.other: the Bull or cattle of many species
relations.myth: Joint veneration of Moon and cattle
relations.note: Māh is worshipped jointly with the many-specied cattle originating through lunar purification.

relations.myth: Ahriman’s assault on the primordial Bull
relations.note: Māh’s preservation of bovine seed indirectly defeats Ahriman’s attempted destruction of animal life.
Māh is classified among Vohu Manah’s subordinate co-workers concerned with beneficial animals.

relations.myth: Regulation of the Moon’s celestial course
relations.note: The fravašis establish or sustain Māh’s course until the final renovation.
Māh passes cosmic happiness onward to Ardwīsūr in a chain of beneficence.
Māh receives cosmic happiness from the obscure being Suk.
Moon and Sun occupy successive heavenly stations and are repeatedly invoked together.
Tištrya and Māh appear together in a ritual catalogue without a narrated encounter.
Mithra and Māh occur together in the same sacrificial catalogue.
Māh and Gōš are co-workers within Vohu Manah’s cattle-oriented divine group.
Māh and Rām are co-workers within Vohu Manah’s subordinate divine group.
The Kushan lunar god Mao is a regional continuation or adaptation of Māh.
Eastern Manichaean tradition reassigns the Iranian Moon name to Jesus in its light-ship cosmology.
